A1.justification: Both PDFs describe STAvatar and contain readable methods, equations, figures, tables, and supplementary materials. Existing content can be matched reliably across layout changes and supplementary renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction and reenactment results on four datasets, component and hyperparameter ablations, and density and training-efficiency analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds learned-offset visualizations and INSTA comparisons with GAGAvatar and LAM-20K.

M1.justification: The UV soft-binding architecture, sampling algorithms, FTC/FPE-AP density control, activation functions, and training losses remain unchanged. The new offset visualizations analyze the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four datasets and 22 identities, retaining reconstruction and cross-identity reenactment coverage. The added baseline comparison reuses INSTA without evaluating STAvatar under a new input scenario.

E2.justification: v3 adds GAGAvatar and LAM-20K as evaluated comparators in supplementary Table 2 and Figure 5. The six original baselines remain in the main and per-identity comparisons.

E3.justification: Reported splits, 512×512 preprocessing, training schedules, FLAME refinement, and PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS metrics remain unchanged. The added INSTA comparison identifies single-image baselines but supplies no separate revised evaluation procedure or detailed settings.

E4.justification: Supplementary Section 3.4 and Figure 4 add a spatial analysis of learned position, rotation, and color offsets across facial and hair regions. Existing ablations, clustering visualizations, Gaussian-count comparisons, and training-efficiency analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new comparison continues reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: New supplementary Table 2 reports INSTA PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS of 21.71/0.8655/0.1292 for LAM-20K and 22.81/0.8942/0.1042 for GAGAvatar. STAvatar's 30.63/0.9587/0.0304 and all retained quantitative table values are unchanged. Supplementary Figures 4–5 add offset-map findings and qualitative comparisons.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, equations, sampling pseudocode, silhouette-coefficient formulation, and summed-area-table derivation are retained. The added discussion introduces no new formal assumptions, proofs, or mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about UV-adaptive soft binding, temporal density control, reconstruction fidelity, and training efficiency. The supplementary additions do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: New supplementary Sections 3.4–3.5 interpret spatially concentrated offsets as compensating for details absent from FLAME. They also explicitly acknowledge the requirement for monocular video and per-subject training, discussing its applicability and fidelity trade-off against generalizable single-image methods.

D1.justification: v3 replaces the future code-release statement and earlier project address with a current project-availability statement and updated address. The PDFs do not establish that code was released. Existing implementation and hyperparameter disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including PC-Talk, SRM-Hair, HRAvatar, and GUAVA, and expands supplementary positioning against generalizable reconstruction through GAGAvatar, LAM, and other cited works. The original related-work arguments and novelty framing remain largely intact.

P1.justification: v3 updates author and affiliation information, adds acknowledgements, and expands the supplementary overview with two new subsections. Existing self- and cross-reenactment sections are renumbered; the main scientific narrative remains largely verbatim.

P2.justification: v3 adds supplementary offset-map and baseline-comparison figures plus a comparison table. Existing figures and tables are retained with some relocation, renumbering, typography, and plot-legend adjustments; the overall visual organization remains similar.

improvement.justification: v3 improves interpretability through the offset-map analysis and makes applicability limits more explicit through its discussion of video input and per-subject training. The added GAGAvatar/LAM comparison broadens context, although differing input regimes and sparse setup details limit its conclusions. These are useful, bounded gains; the method and retained results are unchanged.
